name: The Delve
setup: The ruin has been settling for four hundred years and it has opinions about being entered. This is not a fight; it is a negotiation with a building that is losing an argument with gravity.

stages.objective: Get down into the first gallery without bringing the shaft with you
stages.change: You are in, and the way you came is narrower than it was.

stages.objective: Cross the gallery floor, which is a lid rather than a floor
stages.change: The gallery is crossed. Something below registered the weight.

stages.objective: Leave, carrying whatever you came for
stages.change: Out, with the ruin substantially more closed than you found it.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⚠️ *'THIS IS NOT A FIGHT; IT IS A NEGOTIATION.'* ⛔ A party negotiates worse: four hundred years of settling answers to load and vibration, and three people are more of both. ⚑ The ruin has opinions about being entered and a party is a larger entering.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⛔ Whether you can move as one weight. ⚠️ Splitting up is correct here and it is also how you lose someone.
party.foldNote: ⚑ A folded SHAPE ally can hold what is going — the clearest case in the corpus for bringing a mason.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. Every encounter in the corpus was written when a fight was ONE PERSON AGAINST ONE OPPONENT. ⚑ R36 makes a party member fight from their own sheet; R36a caps three acting fully and folds the rest. ⚠️ THE CLAUSE IS ADDITIVE — no prose changed. It is what a GM reads when more than one person is present.
